source_ref: osf.io/4b85w data paper/codebooks/processed_data_dictionary.csv (Variable, Section Header, Field_Type, Field_Label, possible values) -- Oxford ARC study; Parsons, Todorovic, Lim, Songco & Fox (2022) data and protocol paper
note: Level-1 source with no mapping inference at all. The Oxford ARC data paper ships codebooks/processed_data_dictionary.csv, one row per variable, and all 44 live item codes appear in its Variable column verbatim; item_text is that row's Field_Label, section_prompt its Section Header. The codes are self-describing besides (activity_exercise_outside, media_why_tv_news), so a permutation could not survive a reading. The table pools two response formats and the dictionary distinguishes them by Field_Type, which is why option_text is populated for some items and not others: 36 'radio' items carry the labels '1, Never | 2, Rarely | 3, Sometimes | 4, Often | 5, Always' and ship all five; the 8 'text' items are average hours per day, a free numeric quantity rather than a category, so their levels 0-5 are hours and carry no option label. That gives 180 labelled option cells and 48 deliberately blank. Two sections are carried: the hours block under 'Please report the average number of hours per day...' and the reasons block under 'please rate how much you did this activity for the following reasons'. instructions is empty because the dictionary gives no whole-table framing distinct from those two section headers. audit_batch.R WARNs on this table and both halves are the instrument, not a defect: the 36 reason items fall into six clusters of six with near-identical n inside each (2,264-2,304 up to 6,193-6,277) because each medium's six reasons were shown only to respondents who used that medium, and the blank-option_text half is the hours-per-day format described above.
public_note: 44 items on two response formats. The 36 reason items run 1 = Never to 5 = Always. The 8 remaining items ask for average hours per day, so their 0-5 values are hours rather than scale points and carry no option labels.

note: The three additional questions are reproduced verbatim in the article's S1 File under 'Part 4 : Additional questions', followed by 'Participants gave a single answer to each item.' source_ref: Gratz & Roemer (2004), 'Multidimensional Assessment of Emotion Regulation and Dysregulation', J Psychopathol Behav Assess 26:41-54, Table III (all 36 items) and p.44 (response anchors); item codes and used resp levels from the live table; DERS_SUM_POST from the deposit, osf.io/9jgxs 'amps psychometric eval.csv'. Study paper: 10.1007/s12671-023-02144-1 (PMC12959836).
note: Wording is the instrument's own publication; the mapping is reconstructed and verified on three routes (see verify_paampsmartsud_saba_2023_ders.R). THE NUMBERING TRAP: Table III numbers items in the original 41-item pool, not the published 36-item numbering the deposit uses. Pool items 2, 11, 13, 18 and 36 were dropped and the survivors renumbered 1..36 in ascending order; shipping Table III's numbers as-is would have misassigned most of the scale. That renumbering is what was tested: it places the article's 11 reverse-scored items on exactly positions 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, 20, 22, 24, 34, which the deposit's own DERS_SUM_POST independently pins (dropping DERS_37_POST and reversing those 11 reproduces the total for all 90 complete rows, where no other single-column drop exceeds 42 of 90 and no-reverse scoring matches 6). DERS_37_POST is therefore NOT a scored DERS item and its wording is unknown, so it ships with empty item_text and empty option_text rather than being guessed; its resp rows are present so the item and resp sets still match the live table. DEVIATIONS: two PDF rendering artefacts were normalised in the text -- the fi/fl ligatures (U+FB01/U+FB02) to ASCII, and the typographic apostrophe (U+2019) to "'" -- neither is a feature of the administered form. Response anchors are Gratz & Roemer's own, including their percentage bands; note that the study paper renders the low anchor as 'never' where the instrument's publication says 'almost never (0-10%)', and the instrument was followed. No administered instruction text was recovered from either the deposit or the two papers, so instructions and section_prompt are empty; the study describes a 30-day reporting window and Gratz & Roemer describe the task as indicating 'how often the items apply to themselves', but neither reproduces what respondents were shown. RIGHTS: cleared under the corrected test settled in #1945 -- the DERS carries no licence fee and no quotable no-redistribution clause (APA PsycTests 10.1037/t01029-000 is behind SSO and could not be quoted either way), so silence is permission. Supersedes this table's earlier blocked note, which was held partly on the superseded stricter reading. On DERS_37_POST specifically: it is not identifiable, but it does sit in the same administered matrix -- n = 180 responses and an observed range of 1-5, identical to all 36 scored items, with mean 1.86. That is why its resp rows are kept; the option labels are still left blank rather than inferred from the block, since an unidentified item could carry its own anchors.
public_note: The 36-item Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale administered post-intervention. resp runs 1-5 over Gratz & Roemer's anchors, stored RAW -- the 11 reverse-keyed items (DERS_1, _2, _6, _7, _8, _10, _17, _20, _22, _24, _34_POST) are not pre-reversed, so reverse them before summing. DERS_37_POST is in the response table but is not a scored DERS item and its wording is not recorded anywhere in the deposit or the papers; it ships with no item text rather than a guess. Its observed responses do span 1-5 with the same respondent count as the scored items, so it appears to have been administered on the same grid.
